liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Reviewer describes the opening version as brilliant and energetic [14]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Reviewer highlights a rare three-minute "Feeling Groovy" jam beginning at the 11:20 mark [3]

## The recordings

- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.jackson.smith.94377.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 29 songs; 216 min; rated 4.38/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Recording is a multi-generation transfer, cleaned and adapted, though it contains noticeable hiss; Listener suggests equalizing playback to improve the sound quality of this specific recording; Reviewer argues the show sounds fantastic, rejecting claims of poor quality or excessive hiss [4][5][8][10]
- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.thecore.4640.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 195 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: First couple notes are clipped, sounding like a patched splice or dropout; Minor splice occurs at roughly 19:00, with frequent distortion from Keith's piano [2]

## Around the show

- Bob Weir later described the audience as the coldest and stiffest he ever played [3]
- Venue described as a concrete dump with pillars blocking sight lines, yet packed with thousands [10]
- Jerry told the crowd they were making a record, exciting the audience present [14]
- Reviewer claims this Newcastle performance puts nearly everything else from 1972 to shame [12]
- Reviewer notes most sources list Brokedown Palace as the encore, not One More Saturday Night [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.jackson.smith.94377.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rex Jackson; transferred by Matt Smith and Jamie Waddell; source: SBD > Master Reel [1]
- **gd1972-04-11.sbd.thecore.4640.shnf**: source: SBD>MC>D>CD [2]. Also: Sound Forge and CD Wave used to edit blemishes, adjust levels, and reduce distortion [2]
